name: ARM_Request

query.description: Optional query string parameters (api-version is added automatically).

confirm.description: Must be exactly true. Acknowledges that this call changes live Azure resources. There is no dry run: if this is set, the change is made.

name: Graph_GET
title: Graph GET
description: Read any Microsoft Graph endpoint. Use the specific Entra tools when one exists. Covers users, groups, devices, directory roles, applications, service principals, Intune deviceManagement, and audit logs. CLI: `az rest --method get --url https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/<path>`.

path.description: Graph path beginning with '/', e.g. '/users' or '/deviceManagement/managedDevices'.

query.description: OData query parameters, e.g. {"$filter": "accountEnabled eq true", "$select": "id,displayName"}.

consistency_eventual.description: Send ConsistencyLevel: eventual. Required for $count, $search, and some $filter forms.

name: Graph_Request
title: Graph Request
description: Escape hatch: write to any Microsoft Graph endpoint (POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE). Creates and updates users, group membership, app registrations, Conditional Access policies, and Intune configuration. DELETE needs the destructive gate. Permissions are bounded by the signed-in identity's Graph roles. CLI: `az rest --method <post|patch|put|delete> --url https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/<path>`.

method.description: HTTP method. For reads use Graph_GET.

confirm.description: Must be exactly true. Acknowledges that this call changes live Azure resources. There is no dry run: if this is set, the change is made.

timespan.description: ISO 8601 range 'start/end', e.g. 2026-07-07T00:00:00Z/2026-07-08T00:00:00Z. Defaults to the last hour.

interval.description: ISO 8601 duration granularity, e.g. PT5M or PT1H.

aggregation.description: Comma-separated aggregations: Average, Minimum, Maximum, Total, Count.

query.description: KQL query, e.g. 'Heartbeat | summarize count() by Computer | limit 10'.

timespan.description: Optional ISO 8601 duration or range, e.g. P1D or 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z/2026-07-08T00:00:00Z.

name: Az_CLI
title: Azure CLI (Read)
description: Run any read-only Azure CLI command: every `az ... list`, `show`, `get-*`, `check-*`, and `az rest --method get` against an Azure endpoint. This is the whole CLI surface for reads, one-to-one with `az`; use it for anything the dedicated tools do not cover. Output is JSON unless you pass -o. Commands that change something, or that return keys, connection strings or secrets, are refused here and run through Az_CLI_Run instead. Use Az_CLI_Help to look up arguments. CLI: `az <group> <command> [args]`.

args.description: The words after "az", one per element, e.g. ["vm", "list", "-g", "my-rg"]. Preferred over command: no quoting needed.

command.description: The same as one string, e.g. "vm list -g my-rg --query \"[].name\"". A leading "az" is ignored. Quotes group words; nothing is expanded.

subscription_id.description: Adds --subscription <id> when the command does not already carry one. Leave unset for commands without that argument (az ad ...).

timeout_seconds.description: Kill the command after this many seconds. Default 120. Prefer --no-wait for long-running operations.

name: Az_CLI_Run
title: Azure CLI (Run)
description: Run any Azure CLI command, including creates, updates, deletes and commands that return credentials: one-to-one with `az`. Each command is classified before it runs: writes need write mode; disruptive verbs (delete, purge, stop, deallocate, restart, regenerate, revoke, ...) also need the destructive gate. Prompts cannot be answered, so pass --yes where the CLI asks for confirmation, and --no-wait for long operations. Arguments starting with '@' (local files) are refused. CLI: `az <group> <command> [args]`.

args.description: The words after "az", one per element, e.g. ["vm", "list", "-g", "my-rg"]. Preferred over command: no quoting needed.

command.description: The same as one string, e.g. "vm list -g my-rg --query \"[].name\"". A leading "az" is ignored. Quotes group words; nothing is expanded.

subscription_id.description: Adds --subscription <id> when the command does not already carry one. Leave unset for commands without that argument (az ad ...).

timeout_seconds.description: Kill the command after this many seconds. Default 120. Prefer --no-wait for long-running operations.

confirm.description: Must be exactly true. Acknowledges that this call changes live Azure resources. There is no dry run: if this is set, the change is made.

name: Az_CLI_Help
title: Azure CLI Help
description: Show `az <group> [<command>] --help`: the subgroups, commands, arguments and examples, straight from the installed CLI. Use it before Az_CLI or Az_CLI_Run when unsure of a command's arguments. CLI: `az <group> [<command>] --help`.

command.description: Command path, e.g. ["vm"] or ["network", "nsg", "rule", "create"]. Empty for the top-level groups.

name: View_Estate
title: Azure Estate
description: Interactive subscription overview: resource counts by type and region, resource groups by size, unhealthy resources, Advisor recommendations by category and impact, the Defender secure score, and month-to-date cost by service. Read-only. Reads Resource Graph, Resource Health, Advisor, Defender and Cost Management in parallel; a source the identity cannot read is reported as a note and the rest still renders. The same data is returned as JSON for hosts without MCP Apps.

subscription_id.description: Azure subscription id. Omit to use the configured default or the az default subscription.

name: View_Virtual_Machines
title: Virtual Machines
description: Interactive virtual machine board: every VM with its power state, size, OS, region and resource group, filterable and sortable, with Start, Deallocate and Restart buttons. Read-only to open. The buttons call Start_VM, Stop_VM and Restart_VM with confirm: true, so the write and destructive gates apply to each click. The same data is returned as JSON for hosts without MCP Apps.

subscription_id.description: Azure subscription id. Omit to use the configured default or the az default subscription.

resource_group.description: Only VMs in this resource group.

name: View_Web_Apps
title: Web Apps
description: Interactive App Service board: every web app and function app with its state, kind, default host name, HTTPS-only setting, region and resource group, with Start, Stop and Restart buttons. Read-only to open. The buttons call Start_Web_App, Stop_Web_App and Restart_Web_App with confirm: true, so the gates apply to each click. The same data is returned as JSON for hosts without MCP Apps.

subscription_id.description: Azure subscription id. Omit to use the configured default or the az default subscription.

resource_group.description: Only apps in this resource group.

name: View_Costs
title: Azure Costs
description: Interactive cost view: total actual cost for the period, a daily trend, cost by service and by resource group, and budgets with their current spend. Read-only. Needs Cost Management Reader (or Reader) on the subscription. The same data is returned as JSON for hosts without MCP Apps.

subscription_id.description: Azure subscription id. Omit to use the configured default or the az default subscription.

name: View_Resources
title: Resource Explorer
description: Interactive resource explorer: every resource in a subscription (or one resource group, or of one type) with type, region, SKU and tags, filterable and sortable. Selecting a row loads its full ARM document through Get_Resource. Read-only. The same data is returned as JSON for hosts without MCP Apps.

subscription_id.description: Azure subscription id. Omit to use the configured default or the az default subscription.

resource_group.description: Only resources in this resource group.

resource_type.description: Only this ARM type, e.g. microsoft.storage/storageaccounts.

max_rows.description: Most resources to read. Default 5000; the result says when it was cut short.

name: View_Security
title: Security Posture
description: Interactive security posture: Defender for Cloud secure score with the controls losing the most points, active Defender alerts by severity, Advisor security recommendations, and Azure Policy non-compliance. Read-only. Sources the identity cannot read (no Defender plan, no policy reader) are reported as notes. The same data is returned as JSON for hosts without MCP Apps.

subscription_id.description: Azure subscription id. Omit to use the configured default or the az default subscription.
